Foreign-owned stores on U.S. military bases are a glaring vulnerability. The America First Investment Policy explicitly restricts foreign adversary access to critical infrastructure and strategic sectors—yet here we are, with PRC-linked entities operating on installations meant to protect national security. 

This isn’t just about supplements; it’s about systemic failure to enforce existing safeguards against espionage and data harvesting. CFIUS should’ve blocked these ventures under Section 6 of the 2025 Investment Policy Memorandum, which bars adversarial investments in sensitive areas. 

Shut them down, audit all base vendors, and prioritize American-owned suppliers. Troops deserve security, not surveillance disguised as retail.
